notes: Seven editorial fixtures for prototype testing, not a production calendar. In a public launch use a reviewed, explicit date-to-scenario schedule.

scenarios.contextForEditor: Late Carboniferous, ~310 million years ago, lowland coal swamp in what is now Euramerica.
clues: You wake beneath a ceiling of green. Warm mist clings to your skin, and the ground gives beneath your feet like a soaked sponge.
Water threads through a forest of strangely patterned trunks. There is no birdsong, only the faint splash of something moving in the shallows.
Towering clubmosses and horsetails crowd the light. You search the undergrowth for a single flower and find none.
A dragonfly-like hunter cuts through the humid air, its strange wings stretching more than half a meter across.
A huge, many-legged arthropod moves through the fallen vegetation. Amphibious creatures wait along the dark pools.
These swamp forests will leave immense coal seams behind. You are standing roughly 310 million years before your own time.
scenarios.epilogue: The Carboniferous Period lasted roughly 359 to 299 million years ago. Vast swamp forests helped form major coal deposits, while large arthropods and early land vertebrates occupied a very different Earth.
scenarios.visualBrief: Begin with indistinct humid green silhouettes. Later reveal striated lycopsid trunks, then an insect-like flyer, then the forest floor. Never depict identifying organisms before their textual clues.

scenarios.contextForEditor: United States urban nightlife, late 1920s, during Prohibition.
clues: You wake to the clatter of traffic and the smell of rain rising from warm pavement. Music leaks from somewhere below the street.
A newsboy calls out headlines while a motorcar squeezes past a streetcar. The city seems intent on moving faster than its own shadows.
A voice crackles from a radio in a shop window. Nearby, a woman with a sharply bobbed haircut laughs beneath a cloche hat.
After dark, a brass horn pulls you toward an unmarked basement door. Someone on the other side asks you for a word you do not know.
Inside, the band is playing jazz and the drinks are poured discreetly. The club has plenty of customers, but no lawful right to sell liquor.
The country has banned alcohol, yet its cities are alive with speakeasies, new dances, and the restless confidence of the Jazz Age.
scenarios.epilogue: The 1920s in the United States were marked by Prohibition, the growth of radio, changing urban culture, and a vibrant jazz scene. The era was also shaped by major social tensions and inequalities beyond the nightlife remembered today.
scenarios.visualBrief: First show wet cobblestones, indistinct downtown buildings and a glowing basement window. Only later reveal period-specific fashions, radio set and jazz-club details.

scenarios.contextForEditor: Late Jurassic, ~150 million years ago, vegetated North American floodplain.
clues: You wake beside a broad river. The air smells of wet earth, and distant thunder rolls across a flat green horizon.
Conifers and cycads crowd the banks. There is no familiar meadow grass, and no flowering shrub to break the endless green.
The earth trembles with slow, heavy footsteps. Far away, something tall moves above the treetops, bending branches as it feeds.
A long-necked dinosaur emerges along the water, its massive body moving with a patience that makes you feel very small.
Another animal crosses a patch of sun, its back edged with tall bony plates. The river plain is ruled by sauropods and their armored neighbors.
You have traveled roughly 150 million years into Earth’s past. These giants flourish long before the last great dinosaur extinction.
scenarios.epilogue: During the Jurassic Period, roughly 201 to 145 million years ago, many dinosaur groups diversified. Forests included conifers, cycads and ferns, while enormous sauropods roamed some floodplains.
scenarios.visualBrief: Begin as generic floodplain with mist, add conifer details with clue 2, first indistinct huge silhouette with clue 3, reveal sauropod only with clue 4 and plated dinosaur only with clue 5.

scenarios.contextForEditor: United States, July 1969, lunar landing television coverage.
clues: You wake to the hum of a television in the next room. Outside, summer heat settles over a neighborhood of small front lawns.
A transistor radio plays popular music with a sharp electric edge. In the paper, images of demonstrations sit beside reports from a distant war.
Inside a school, brightly colored diagrams show rockets and the planets. Children argue about whether people will ever really cross the space between worlds.
At dinner, the grown-ups talk about astronauts as if they were neighbors. A distant rivalry between two superpowers seems to reach all the way into the sky.
Families gather around television sets to watch a spacecraft approach the Moon. The grainy picture is carried into millions of living rooms.
It is July 1969. A human being is about to step onto another world, and nearly everyone with a television is watching.
scenarios.epilogue: The 1960s saw the Space Race culminate in Apollo 11’s first crewed Moon landing in July 1969, alongside profound political and cultural change in the United States.
scenarios.visualBrief: Start inside an indistinct mid-century living room, then add transistor radio, rocket school diagram, and finally a tiny monochrome TV image of lunar terrain only at clue 5.

scenarios.contextForEditor: Late Devonian, ~375 million years ago, coastal shallows and emerging vegetation.
clues: You wake at the edge of a shallow estuary. The tide leaves shining pools among the mud, and the wind smells sharply of salt.
The land is surprisingly bare in places, but strange stands of early trees rise along the water. Their shadows fall across soil that seems newly made.
The shallows are alive with fish of unfamiliar shapes, some enclosed in plates of bony armor. The water feels far more crowded than the shore.
A broad-headed creature braces itself in the shallows on sturdy, limb-like fins. It does not quite belong to the sea or the land you recognize.
Some of the first forests spread inland while early four-limbed vertebrates begin their evolutionary story. Fish dominate an age of remarkable change.
You have arrived around 375 million years ago, in a period often nicknamed the Age of Fishes.
scenarios.epilogue: The Devonian Period, roughly 419 to 359 million years ago, witnessed the diversification of fishes, the rise of early forests, and major transitions in vertebrate evolution.
scenarios.visualBrief: Start with mist over tidal pools, then add primitive trees, armored fish in clear water and, late, a fin-limbed shoreline inhabitant.

scenarios.contextForEditor: Oklahoma Panhandle, April 1935, Dust Bowl during Great Depression.
clues: You wake to an orange light at the window. The house is still, but the air tastes faintly of earth.
Outside, a field lies bare and cracked. At the fence line, wind has heaped the loose soil into drifts as if it were winter snow.
A family has tucked rags around the doors, yet fine dust settles on the table. Someone speaks quietly about another failed crop.
A neighbor mentions leaving for California. Work is scarce everywhere, and the farm has become harder to defend with every season.
By afternoon a wall of darkness rises across the plains. The wind turns the sky black in a storm people have begun calling a black blizzard.
It is the middle of the Great Depression. Across the southern Plains, drought and blowing topsoil have given this disaster its name: the Dust Bowl.
scenarios.epilogue: The Dust Bowl devastated the Great Plains in the 1930s. Severe drought, exposed topsoil and economic hardship drove destructive storms and forced many families to migrate.
scenarios.visualBrief: Show a farmhouse window with diffuse amber light, then cracked soil and drifting dust; delay the dramatic black storm front until clue 5.

scenarios.contextForEditor: Late Cretaceous western North America, ~68 million years ago.
clues: You wake beside a river in a warm lowland forest. Small flying creatures stir in the light, and the damp air carries the scent of leaves.
Unlike some ancient landscapes, this one has flowering plants among its ferns and conifers. The world looks strange, but unexpectedly familiar.
Across the water, enormous animals move through the undergrowth. One pushes a broad, beaked head through the foliage.
A three-horned giant stands at the forest edge, turning its great shield-like frill toward a sudden sound.
The branches shake as a massive two-legged predator emerges, its powerful jaws dwarfing its small forelimbs.
You are near the end of the dinosaurs’ long reign, around 68 million years ago. A catastrophe in the geologically near future will change life on Earth.
scenarios.epilogue: The Cretaceous Period ended about 66 million years ago. Flowering plants spread widely during this period, and Late Cretaceous ecosystems included Triceratops and Tyrannosaurus rex before the end-Cretaceous mass extinction.
scenarios.visualBrief: Begin with lightly wooded river, reveal flowers clue 2, indistinct dinosaur shapes clue 3, three-horned creature clue 4, large tyrannosaur clue 5. Never show dinosaurs in initial key art.
